drc.description: Run the stock KLayout DRC deck of the PDK on a layout and give a typed verdict. Inputs: gds (the layout, relative to the design root), cell (the top cell), rule_set (optional; a rule set of the technology pack, for example main or full; the default is the default set of the pack), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK), max_examples (optional, default 3). The adapter reconciles the verdict with the exit code of the deck and the marker database: the counts are measured only when the deck wrote a complete marker database and its exit code agrees with the marker count. Else the run is 'not run': markers and rules_violated are failed, the response is failed, and an error diagnostic gives the reason and the last lines of the deck log. A printed summary without a complete report is not a result. Measurements: markers (all markers), rules_violated (the number of rules with markers), runtime_s. Diagnostics: one error per violated rule, largest count first, with the rule name, the count, the rule description of the deck, the cells of the markers and up to max_examples marker boxes in µm (cell coordinates). work/drc.json has the full table: each rule with its description, count, cells and all boxes. The outputs have the marker database and the deck log. Use it instead of a DRC shell script, so that each run is recorded.

lvs.description: Run the stock KLayout LVS deck of the PDK: compare a layout with a reference netlist, and give a typed verdict. Inputs: gds, cell (the top cell), netlist (the reference netlist, relative to the design root, in the netlist form of the pack), pins (optional; the pins of the top cell in order), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK). A match is given only from a complete LVS database: the deck log has the match text of the pack, the exit code is a code of a completed run, the LVS database exists and loads in KLayout, and its compare status is a match. Else the result is 'not run' (all counts failed, the response failed), with an error diagnostic that names the condition that failed. A printed match from a run that crashed or left a truncated database is not a match. Measurements: match (1 or 0), unmatched_devices, unmatched_nets, unmatched_pins (the pins of the input pins that are not pins of the extracted top circuit or of the reference circuit, or are in a different order than in the reference netlist; the extracted circuit sorts its pins by name, so the order is the order of the reference netlist), runtime_s. On a mismatch, error diagnostics give the circuits, devices and nets that do not match (up to 10 each); work/lvs.json has all of them and the pin check. Each pin problem is a warning, also on a match. The outputs have the extracted netlist, the LVS database and the deck log. Use it instead of an LVS shell script, so that each run is recorded.
